title: Liu-Montgomery Sharp Cycle Length Constant
description: Formalizes the sharp constant (1/2) in the Gyárfás-Komlós-Szemerédi theorem: for graphs with average degree d, the sum of reciprocal cycle lengths is at least (1/2 - o(1)) log d. Proves tightness via bipartite construction analysis.

meta.author: Liu, Montgomery (2023)
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: liu_montgomery_sharp — the (1/2 - o(1)) log d lower bound from Liu-Montgomery (JAMS 2023, 43 pages). All computational results (harmonic sums, bipartite cycle sums, tightness) fully verified.
originalContributions: evenHarmonic_eq_half_harmonic: even harmonic sum equals half the full harmonic sum
sharp_constant_achieved: confirms 1/2 is the achieved constant
bipartite_is_even + odd_cycle_increases_sum: structural proof of tightness

overview.historicalContext: Gyárfás, Komlós, and Szemerédi proved in the 1980s that graphs with high average degree contain cycles of many different lengths, with the sum of reciprocal cycle lengths growing at least logarithmically. The optimal constant in this bound remained open until Hong Liu and Richard Montgomery's 2023 paper in JAMS, where they proved the sharp constant is $1/2$: $\sum 1/a_i \ge (1/2 - o(1)) \log d$. This file formalizes the tightness analysis, showing that complete bipartite graphs $K_{m,m}$ achieve exactly $(1/2)(H(m) - 1) \sim (1/2) \ln m$ because they have only even-length cycles.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the sharp constant $1/2$ in the Gyárfás-Komlós-Szemerédi theorem and prove tightness via bipartite construction analysis.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization develops harmonic sum infrastructure, then analyzes the cycle structure of $K_{m,m}$: its cycles have lengths $\{4, 6, \ldots, 2m\}$, contributing $\sum_{j=2}^m 1/(2j) = (1/2)(H(m) - 1)$. The tightness argument decomposes cycle sums into even and odd parts, showing bipartite graphs minimize the sum (having no odd-cycle contributions). The Liu-Montgomery lower bound is axiomatized from the published result.
keyInsights: The constant 1/2 arises because complete bipartite graphs (the minimizers) have only even-length cycles 2j, contributing 1/(2j) = (1/2)(1/j)
Non-bipartite graphs have additional odd-cycle contributions (1/(2j+1) > 0), so they cannot achieve a smaller reciprocal sum
The decomposition into even and odd cycle sums reduces the tightness argument to a simple algebraic fact about harmonic numbers
The Liu-Montgomery lower bound matches the bipartite upper bound asymptotically, confirming 1/2 as sharp

sections.title: Part I: Partial Harmonic Sums
sections.summary: Defines H(m), even harmonic, shifted harmonic. Proves evenHarmonic = (1/2)H(m), nonnegativity, and monotonicity.

sections.title: Part II: Complete Bipartite Graph Cycle Lengths
sections.summary: Defines bipartiteCycleRecipSum for K_{r,s}. Proves K_{m,m} sum = (1/2)(H(m)-1).

sections.title: Part III: The Sharp Constant (Axiomatized)
sections.summary: Liu-Montgomery theorem axiomatized: Σ 1/aᵢ ≥ (1/2 - ε) log d for sufficiently large d.

sections.title: Part IV: Odd Cycle Analysis
sections.summary: Decomposes reciprocal sum into even and odd contributions. Proves odd cycles add strictly positive terms.

sections.title: Part V: Tightness of the 1/2 Constant
sections.summary: Proves bipartite graphs achieve the 1/2 constant and non-bipartite graphs cannot do better.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the tightness analysis for the Liu-Montgomery sharp constant $1/2$ in the cycle reciprocal sum theorem. All computational results are fully verified; the Liu-Montgomery lower bound itself is axiomatized from the 43-page JAMS 2023 paper.
conclusion.implications: This verifies that the natural barrier for cycle reciprocal sums comes from bipartite graphs, connecting extremal graph theory to harmonic analysis. The even/odd decomposition technique is reusable for other cycle spectrum problems.
openQuestions: Can the Liu-Montgomery lower bound be formalized, at least for special graph families?
What is the sharp constant for graphs of given girth (minimum cycle length)?
